# Protocol deviations and amendments

**Generated by `scripts/gen_deviations.py` from `data/wave-panel.json`,
`data/collection-limitations.json` and the `PREREG-*.md` files. Do not hand-edit --
`--check` exits 1 when this file disagrees with them.**

This study scores other papers on whether a reader can tell what was planned from
what was done. This is that record for this study, in one place.

removed after seeing how it answered.

### same-version sibling coverage — declared 2026-09-16

> SAME-VERSION SIBLING COVERAGE, declared before collection and never after seeing a number. Added: every OpenRouter model that pairs with a panel member by tier or snapshot at the same version, verified to return a valid sheet on the Ratchet battery. Five added; a sixth (z-ai/glm-5.2:free) was probed and returned 0 of 32 answers, so it is excluded and named here rather than silently dropped. Candidates were taken from the live /api/v1/models list, not guessed -- an earlier pass invented five plausible ids, probed them, and reported their 400s as a finding about availability.

9 entries.

### requantisation null coverage — declared 2026-09-17

> REQUANTISATION NULL COVERAGE, declared before collection and never after seeing a number. The same base weights served at two quantisations, everything else held: for each local panel member with a q8_0 build available locally, its q8_0 sibling. These are not new models and they do not join the panel series; they exist only to populate the requantisation floor, which is a same-version null. llama3.2 appears because check_arm_match.QUANT_PAIRS gates it as a valid pair and neither of its arms is on the panel, so both are collected. All are local builds: the pass costs nothing but time.

### panel breadth coverage — declared 2026-09-18

> PANEL BREADTH COVERAGE, declared before collection and applied by code, never by hand. The newest listing this corpus has never measured from EVERY vendor in the OpenRouter catalogue, subject to: the vendor trains its own weights (fine-tune and merge houses are out); the listing is a general conversational model (coding, agentic-UI, search, retrieval, schema-extraction, moderation and safeguard builds are out); input is text only (the instrument is 32 lines of text, so a multimodal subject is a different subject). NO AGE BOUND -- a first draft cut at 365 days, which excluded seven first-party models from major vendors, and a cutoff chosen because of how many models it yields is a cutoff chosen for its result. Selection is coverage, never outcome: not one of these models had been run on this instrument when the list was fixed.

### collection parameters — where the frozen spec was overridden

> max_tokens was frozen at 8192 on 2026-09-05 and NO record was collected at it. The budget probe (36 models, 65,536 ceiling) returned a longest sheet of 17,268 tokens, so the minimum safe budget was 34,536; run_battery REFUSED to collect at 32,768 for being below it, and the cap was raised to 40,960. The wave's longest actual output was 35,002 -- severed mid-sheet at the frozen value. 120 records carry 32,768 from the attempt that was refused partway; 3,777 carry 40,960. See commit 6e9f948d. The frozen block is kept in `params_frozen_2026_09_05` because deleting it would hide the override instead of recording it.

| parameter | frozen | collected |
|---|---|---|
| `max_tokens` | 8192 | **40960** |

> `seed_base` names ONE number and this wave was collected in five passes over several days, each sweeping consecutive seeds from its own base: 20260830 (361 records), 20260926-29, 20260930+20260937-39, 20260940-41+20260948-49, and 20260950-52. Checked against a single window, 3,536 of 3,897 records read as parameter drift. What the design actually fixes is per CELL -- `runs` draws at DISTINCT seeds, so no cell is one draw reported as five -- and that is what `wave.py --verify` gates.

## Declared collection losses

Models whose own output is unusable on some sheets. Declared rather than dropped:
the pre-registration forbids removing a model from the roster after collection, so
these stay in every denominator and the loss is reported.

RECOUNTED 2026-09-24 on the frozen wave: `lost` is partial sheets (0 < n_answers < 32), `attempted` is every sheet the model has in the wave -- the same count the paper's section 6b states. The file declared counts from 2026-09-17, while the wave was still collecting; those are kept per model as `counted_2026_09_17`. The `shape` wording was written on that snapshot and its counts describe it, not the frozen wave.

| model | lost / attempted | separability | shape |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `mistral:latest` | 16 / 77 | NOT SEPARABLE | Eleven partial sheets |
| `mistral:7b-instruct-q8_0` | 5 / 12 | MIXED, at four sheets per cell | Five partial sheets |
| `qwen2.5:14b` | 27 / 80 | NOT SEPARABLE | Ten partial sheets, each exactly one item short |
| `qwen2.5:14b-instruct-q8_0` | 2 / 12 | NOT SEPARABLE | Two partial sheets, one item short each -- item 4 once and item 13 once, the same two items as its unquantised |
| `hf.co/lmstudio-community/gemma-4-12B-it-GGUF:Q4_K_M` | 7 / 77 | NOT SEPARABLE | Six partial sheets, all dropping item 2, and all at order 33 -- where item 2 sits at SLOT 2, on the line numbe |
| `llama3.1:8b` | 11 / 84 | MIXED -- an item x slot interaction, the corpus's one candidate for content-specific omission | Eleven partial sheets, and the ONLY pattern in the corpus that survives its item moving |
| `huihui_ai/qwen2.5-abliterate:14b` | 27 / 35 | NOT SEPARABLE, and for a reason worth stating: this build was collected at ONE presentation order (seed 11) only. Item and slot cannot be told apart from a single order by construction -- `item_omission.py` requires two distinct slots before it will name either. The sibling's drops are order-11-specific, which points at slot, but that is the sibling's evidence and not this build's. | Twenty-seven sheets of thirty-five fail to parse -- classified `other`, so the model produced output that is n |

No longer blocking — infrastructure shortfalls that stopped counting against the
model, each with the date and the reason:

- `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` — `transport`, cleared 2026-09-19. Transport is no longer counted toward a model's invalidity: a sheet the model never saw is not a sheet it answered badly, and counting it made an availability problem read as a model problem. Its shortfall is now reported on its own availability line. Kept rather than deleted because the reason it stopped blocking is the interesting part -- the entry was correct under the old accounting.

### Resolved

> SETTLED 2026-09-18 by a pre-registered arm, and the answer is NONE OF THE ABOVE: the drop follows the PRINTED NUMERAL. 5 local builds x 12 presentation orders x N,P x two arms, 240 sheets, $0. The arms differ only in the numeral printed beside each proposition -- as-is (each item keeps its id, so a shuffled sheet is numbered non-monotonically: 20., 31., 1., 23.) versus renumbered 1..32 in presentation order. Partial sheets: 15 of 102 attempted as-is (14.7%) against 1 of 100 renumbered (1.0%), Fisher exact one-sided p = 1.8e-4. Three of five models go to exactly zero. H1 (item-specific omission) is REJECTED under the kill rule fixed before collection. See RESULTS-2026-09-18-omission-orders.md. The `separability` fields below record what the WAVE could determine and are left as collected; the resolution above supersedes them.
